true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. In the list view only the prom rule is available. The Silence menu item is enabled by the Grafana prom abilities, but the drawer still requires a Grafana ruler rule before it renders. As a result, clicking the item toggles state and nothing visible happens.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete menu item can never appear for Grafana rules in the list view (rulerRule is always undefined there)

The Delete menu item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the alert list view the whole point of this PR is that no ruler API calls are made, so `RuleActionsButtons.V2` is rendered with only `promRule` and `rule` (rulerRule) is `undefined`. Even though the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` path can set `canDelete` to true from prom-rule/folder permissions, the `rulerRule &&` guard means the Delete item is never rendered in the list view, so users can no longer delete Grafana-managed rules from the list. The pause menu item at line 123 has the same problem: `canPause` can be true via the grafana ability, but rendering requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, which is false when only a promRule exists. Either the menu items need to work off the promRule (e.g. construct the delete/pause payloads from the prom rule), or the abilities should not report these actions as available.

ModifyExport ability for prom rules excludes recording rules, unlike the ruler-rule path

In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport` is `[isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` where `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. The equivalent ruler-based hook uses `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which matches both alerting and recording Grafana rules. So a Grafana-managed recording rule shows the Export menu in the details view (ruler path) but not in the list view (prom path). If export of recording rules is intended to remain available, use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` here; otherwise the two paths should be made consistent.

Removed coverage for creating/deleting rule states with no replacement

The PR deletes the tests 'should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists', and the entire `matchRules` describe block, and the component no longer has any creating/deleting handling. The behavior change (a just-created rule now simply doesn't appear until Prometheus catches up, and a deleting rule renders fully actionable until it disappears) is a real UX regression risk that is now completely untested — there is no test asserting what the list shows during these eventual-consistency windows.

Template variables are now applied twice in the shard-splitting path

runShardSplitQuery() now maps every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() before delegating to splitQueriesByStreamShard(), but each shard group is then executed via runSplitQuery() (line 163), which after this PR also calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on every target again. So in the sharded path every query is interpolated at least twice (once here, and once per shard group inside runSplitQuery — the updated test even asserts applyTemplateVariables was called 5 times for a single query). Beyond the wasted work, double interpolation is not guaranteed to be idempotent: if a variable's value itself contains a '$'-prefixed token (e.g. a label value like '$foo'), the second pass inside runSplitQuery will re-interpolate it and corrupt the query sent to Loki. Either the interpolation here or in runSplitQuery should be skipped when the queries were already interpolated.

applyTemplateVariables invoked per shard group via runSplitQuery

Because runSplitQuery now unconditionally calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on all targets, the shard-splitting flow (which pre-interpolates in runShardSplitQuery and then calls runSplitQuery once per shard group) re-runs template variable interpolation on every shard sub-request, even though the expressions are already fully interpolated and only differ by the injected __stream_shard__ selector. For dashboards with many template variables this repeats the interpolation/scopedVar resolution work for every shard group; consider interpolating once and passing the results through.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Device limit check is racy: count-then-insert is not atomic

CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit by running CountDevices and then conditionally inserting. Two (or more) concurrent anonymous requests for new devices can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit. On a busy instance with many simultaneous first-time anonymous visitors, the limit can be breached by an arbitrary margin. Enforcement needs to be atomic (e.g., insert guarded by a transaction with a locked count, a UNIQUE/sequence-based cap, or accepting the race and documenting it).
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same race condition: concurrent requests pass the device count check and insert, exceeding the limit. Both suggest a transaction or lock as the fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
ErrDeviceLimitReached aborts anonymous authentication with a raw internal error

TagDevice is now called synchronously in Authenticate, and ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned as the authenticate error. The authn framework will treat this as a failed authentication, so every request from a new anonymous device (once the limit is hit) fails with an unhandled internal error rather than a controlled response (e.g., a 429 or a rendered 'device limit reached' page). The error message 'device limit reached' is also a bare fmt.Errorf with no user-facing wording, and browsers will keep retrying, generating error noise. The authn error handling for this case (status code, redirect behavior, user message) should be explicitly implemented and tested.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same issue. TagDevice is now called synchronously, and ErrDeviceLimitReached causes anonymous authentication to fail once the device limit is reached.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Known device older than 30 days is rejected as 'device limit reached'

When the limit is reached, updateDevice only updates rows whose updated_at is within [now-30d, now+1m] and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when 0 rows are affected. The cleanup job (DeleteDevicesOlderThan) only deletes devices older than 61 days, so a device whose last update is between 30 and 61 days old still occupies a row (and is counted by CountDevices) but cannot be updated — its owner gets a hard 'device limit reached' auth error even though refreshing that existing device would not increase the device count. The update branch should fall back to checking whether the device row exists (and update it) before concluding the limit blocks the request.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when zero rows are affected, even though that result can come from the time-window filter rather than an actual limit. The candidate focuses on the outside-the-window case, which the golden comment explicitly includes. It is the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Local cache is populated before the store write, so a rejected/failed tag is not retried for 29 minutes

tagDeviceUI calls localCache.SetDefault(key, ...) before CreateOrUpdateDevice. If CreateOrUpdateDevice fails (including ErrDeviceLimitReached or a transient DB error), the cache entry remains and subsequent requests from the same device skip the store entirely for up to 29 minutes. With the new synchronous error path this means a transient DB failure during the limit check or insert silently stops device tracking, and TagDevice returns an error to the caller on the first attempt but nil on subsequent ones, giving inconsistent auth behavior. Only populate the cache after a successful store call, or evict on error.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the cache is set before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so after ErrDeviceLimitReached later requests skip the store and get past the limit for 29 minutes. The candidate also says TagDevice returns nil on later attempts, which is the same bypass.

false_positives.candidate:
Extra COUNT query on every device tag when a limit is configured

When deviceLimit > 0, every CreateOrUpdateDevice call performs a full COUNT(*) over anon_device filtered by updated_at before deciding whether to insert. For known devices this count is wasted work (the upsert would have succeeded anyway), and without an index on updated_at this is a table scan per new/refreshing device. Consider only doing the count when the upsert would create a new row, or checking existence of the device_id first.

anonymousDeviceLimit is always serialized and typed inconsistently with the frontend

The Go DTO field AnonymousDeviceLimit is a plain int64 with no omitempty, so the JSON payload always contains "anonymousDeviceLimit": 0 even when no limit is configured, while the TypeScript type in packages/grafana-data declares it as `number | undefined`. Consumers cannot distinguish 'no limit configured' from 'limit of 0' except by the 0-as-unset convention, which is undocumented. Either make it a pointer/omitempty or type the frontend field as a plain number and document the 0 = unlimited convention.

New device_limit option is not added to sample config or docs

The new [auth.anonymous] device_limit setting is parsed but is not added to conf/sample.ini (or defaults.ini comments), so administrators have no discoverable documentation of the option, its default (0 = unlimited), or its semantics (limit over a rolling 30-day window). The PR description also leaves the docs checkbox unchecked.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

true_positives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
@loaded_locales is read outside the load mutex and can be nil on first translate

In `translate`, `@loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` is evaluated without synchronization and without the nil guard that the newly added `ensure_loaded!` has (`@loaded_locales ||= []`). `@loaded_locales` is only initialized in `reload!`; if `translate` is invoked before any `reload!` (or after a direct `load_locale` call from another thread partially completes), the first check raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'include?' for nil`. More generally the check-then-load pattern here is unsynchronized, so two threads can race through `load_locale` — the mutex inside `load_locale` makes the double-load harmless, but the nil read is not protected. `translate` should use the same `@loaded_locales ||= []` guard (or route through `ensure_loaded!`).
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to @loaded_locales being lazily initialized and accessed by concurrent threads without synchronization. The candidate explicitly describes the unsynchronized read outside the mutex, the lazy-init nil issue, and the race between threads.

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are only loaded during controller requests, so fallback translations are missing in jobs/mailers

The new fallback mechanism depends on `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` being called to eagerly load the user's locale, `SiteSetting.default_locale`, and `:en` (because the translate accelerator only lazy-loads `config.locale`). This call was added only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any code path that translates outside of a controller request — Sidekiq/scheduled jobs, email rendering (`UserNotifications`), oneboxing, rake tasks, console — will translate with only the current locale's yml loaded. When a key is missing in that locale, the fallbacks backend looks up the default locale and `:en`, finds nothing loaded, and renders 'translation missing' instead of the English fallback. `ensure_loaded!` needs to be invoked wherever `I18n.locale=` is set (e.g., in the jobs/mailer code paths), not just in the controller.

Custom fallback list drops parent-language fallbacks for regional locales (e.g. pt_BR no longer falls back to pt)

`FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns exactly `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]`. The standard `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` behavior (which `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` provided and this PR removes) decomposes regional locales so that `pt_BR` falls back to `pt` before hitting the default. With this change, a user with locale `pt_BR` (or `zh_TW`, `nb_NO`-style tags) will see English for every key that exists in the base `pt` translation but not in `pt_BR`, which is a user-visible regression for regional locales. The TODO comment even acknowledges per-language ordering is needed; at minimum the list should insert the language-only parent (`locale.to_s.split('_').first`) between the locale and the site default.

FallbackLocaleList recomputes SiteSetting.default_locale on every translation fallback lookup

Because `FallbackLocaleList#[]` is overridden without memoization, every translation lookup that misses the primary locale triggers a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read (which hits the site settings cache/provider) and allocates a new array. Under load this happens per missing-key translation. Consider caching the computed list per locale (e.g., storing into the Hash) and invalidating when the default locale setting changes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh instance, so logs are not recorded

With this change, LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that constructs a TestLogger, passes it to NewLoggerMiddleware, and then inspects InfoLogs will always see zero calls and an empty message — the log entry is recorded on a throwaway logger. true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same bug. record_for_host compares lower(host) against a parameter that is never downcased, so mixed-case hosts fail to match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The candidate says the definitions still load globally, which contradicts the golden's concern about lost fabricators and errors. The core issue, though, is the same.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host values interpolated directly into SQL in migration

The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by interpolating `h`, which comes from the admin-editable `embeddable_hosts` site setting. A host entry containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacters) will produce malformed SQL and abort the migration, and in general this is SQL injection into a migration. Use parameterized execution (e.g. `exec_insert` with binds) or at minimum `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both flag SQL injection from string interpolation of '#{h}' into a SQL INSERT and recommend parameter binding or quoting. The golden places it in the controller and the candidate in a migration, but the identical '#{h}' pattern suggests the same code and issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category setting row is absent

`execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query returns at least one row. Site settings only have rows in the `site_settings` table once they've been changed from the default, so any site that never customized `embed_category` (the common case) will get an empty result set, and `[0]` will be `nil`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil` and aborting the migration. The same pattern is used for `uncategorized_category_id` on line 15. Both lookups need a nil-safe fallback.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: the migration indexes execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking for rows, so it crashes when no embed_category setting exists.

Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) and ideally a unique index in the migration.

Redundant/duplicated authorization filters

Both new admin controllers declare `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff`, but `Admin::AdminController` already enforces admin access, and the routes are additionally wrapped in `AdminConstraint`. More notably `ensure_staff` would allow moderators (staff but not admins) while `AdminConstraint` allows admins — the layering is inconsistent; the controllers should rely on the standard admin controller behavior.

Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

totalPages is off by one when user_count is divisible by limit

totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For a group with exactly 100 members and limit 50, this yields 3 pages when only 2 exist. Since showingLast compares currentPage to totalPages, the user can click "next" past the real last page; the next action sets offset to min(offset + limit, user_count) (i.e. 100), and findMembers then fetches an empty page, showing a blank member list on page "3/3". The computation should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

should_block? reads the record, increments match_count in Ruby, and saves, which loses increments under concurrent signups; more notably it is called from EmailValidator#validate_each, so merely validating a User (not saving) performs a database write with `record.save`, whose failure is silently ignored. true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked email check is case-sensitive and easily bypassed

BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` lookup, and the value passed here is the raw `user.email` attribute, which is stored as the user typed it (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] directly, no downcasing). A blocked address like spammer@example.com can register as Spammer@Example.com and sail past the block list, since PostgreSQL string comparison is case-sensitive. The email should be normalized (e.g. Email.downcase) before the lookup, both here and wherever BlockedEmail records are created.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the email lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block? is case-sensitive, so a blocked address can get past the block by changing its capitalization.

false_positives.candidate:
Blocked emails not enforced on change_email

The new BlockedEmail validation only runs via User's `email` validator, but `change_email` never saves the user with the new email — it only checks uniqueness and creates an email token; the token confirmation path (EmailToken.confirm) updates the address without going through the new validator. An existing account (or one created before an address was blocked) can switch to a blocked email address, defeating the feature. The block check should also be applied in the email-change flow.

rejectedEmails comparison is exact-string and won't match case variants

After a failed signup the server echoes back result.values.email and it is pushed into rejectedEmails; the check `this.get('rejectedEmails').contains(email)` is an exact string comparison against the current accountEmail input. If the user retries with different casing (e.g. Bad@Spam.com vs bad@spam.com) the client-side rejection won't trigger and they'll get another full server round-trip each time. Compare lowercased values.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix, so AMS never calls it

ActiveModelSerializers filters attributes via methods named `include_<attr>?`. The new method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is always serialized — including as `nil` when the user has no website. The intended guard (`website.present?`) has no effect. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify that include_website_name lacks the '?' suffix, which breaks conditional inclusion. The golden comment also raises a secondary string-mutation point, but the main issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name is not declared an untrusted attribute, leaking TL0 users' websites to anonymous viewers

The serializer hides `website` from anonymous viewers of TL0 users via `untrusted_attributes :website, ...`, but the newly added `website_name` attribute is not in that list. Since `website_name` is derived directly from `website`, an anonymous visitor can now read a TL0 user's website host (and path) from the `website_name` field even though `website` itself is correctly suppressed. Add `website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (and fix the missing `?` on its include method).

website_name returns nil for websites without a scheme or with unparseable URLs

`URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for values like `example.com/user` (no scheme — URI parses it as a path, host is nil) or any malformed URL that survives profile validation, causing `website_name` to be nil and the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` to hide the website link entirely even though `model.website` is present. Previously the client-side code displayed `website.split('/')[2]`, which also degraded, but the new serializer should fall back to the raw `website` string instead of returning nil so the link remains visible.

Query string and fragment are dropped from displayed website name

When the domains match, the display value is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, discarding any query string or fragment. A user whose website is `http://example.com/page?id=5` on the same host will see it displayed as `example.com/page`, which no longer represents the actual URL. Include `URI#query`/`fragment` or use `request_uri` when constructing the display path.

Any site able to get a message to the parent window can resize the iframe; the check should compare e.origin against a parsed expected origin.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. i.content can be nil, crashing the hourly feed job

In poll_feed, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: i.content can be nil in RSS feeds, so i.content.scrub raises an error. Both also suggest falling back to description.

false_positives.candidate:
raw_html cook method stores and serves completely unsanitized HTML

`cook` returns `raw` verbatim when cook_method is :raw_html, so posts imported via TopicEmbed.import (feed polling or remote retrieval of the embeddable host) bypass PrettyText/Sanitize entirely and are served as-is (the embed view even does `raw post.cooked`). Any script/event-handler markup in a fetched article or feed item becomes stored XSS on the forum itself, visible in topic pages, digests, and embeds. The imported HTML should be run through Sanitize with an allowlist before storage.

Check-then-create on embed_url races and raises RecordNotUnique

import() does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds a unique index on embed_url, so two concurrent imports of the same URL (hourly PollFeed plus a RetrieveTopic job enqueued from embed#best, which explicitly runs PollFeed and then fetches HTTP itself) will both find no row and one will crash with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique. Rescue RecordNotUnique and fall back to the update path, or use an upsert.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs

Any href/src starting with '/' is prefixed with the article's scheme+host. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg` start with '/', so they are rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, breaking those links/images in every imported post. Check for a leading '//' and skip (or prepend only the scheme) before treating the URL as host-relative.

feed_key is dead code; job does no change detection

feed_key computes a redis key 'feed-modified:<sha>' but nothing ever reads or writes it, and poll_feed re-downloads the feed and re-hashes/re-imports every item every hour. Either wire the key up to skip unchanged feeds (e.g. via If-Modified-Since/ETag or content hash) or remove it; as-is every hourly run re-fetches all items and calls PostRevisor/sha comparisons for each.

Editing an already-shipped migration to add force: true

CreateTopTopics already ran in existing deployments; changing `create_table :top_topics` to `force: true` modifies history. Environments that haven't run it yet (or that replay migrations, e.g. some CI/staging rebuilds after a partially applied state) will silently DROP and recreate the top_topics table, losing all aggregated counts. New behavior should go in a new migration rather than editing an old one.

X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is non-standard and unsupported

`response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'ALLOWALL'` is not a valid X-Frame-Options value (ALLOW-FROM requires a URI and is unsupported in Chrome/Safari; ALLOWALL is ignored entirely by most browsers). The effect is only achieved because an invalid value happens to be ignored — better to explicitly remove the header so the intent is clear and future middleware adding a default DENY doesn't break embeds.

import mutates the caller's contents string

`contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the 'imported from' footer directly to the string passed in. Callers that reuse the buffer (e.g. the Readability document content or anything comparing the original afterwards) get silently modified data, and the sha1 is computed over the mutated value. Duplicate the string (`contents = contents + ...` or `contents.dup`) before appending.

Throws if #discourse-comments element is missing

`comments.appendChild(iframe)` runs without checking that `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` found an element. Site owners paste this snippet into arbitrary templates; if the container is absent or renamed, the script throws and no iframe is created, with no useful error. Bail out early (or log a clear message) when comments is null.

The recurring-cancellation branch (delete all remaining bookings' events across all the user's calendar credentials) was moved inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. For a collective booking with two calendar references, the block that iterates over every user credential and every updated booking is executed once per reference, so each event is deleted N times (and `apiDeletes` collects duplicates). Besides wasted API calls, some providers error on deleting an already-deleted event. Additionally, the inner loop still only deletes `updBooking.references.find(...)` — the first calendar reference per booking — so extra hosts' references are never removed. true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

async forEach makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget and defeats the try/catch

In `Reschedule`, the loop over `bookingRefsFiltered` was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` because `getCalendar` is now async. `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so all `calendar.deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` calls are now unawaited: the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns `true` before deletions finish, and any rejection inside a callback becomes an unhandled promise rejection that the surrounding `try/catch` (which only catches synchronous errors) will never see. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (optionally with per-item catch) so failures are logged and deletions complete before the email is sent.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same problem. forEach with async callbacks leaves the calendar/video deletions unawaited. That causes fire-and-forget behavior and unhandled rejections that the try/catch cannot catch. Both suggest Promise.all with map as the fix.

false_positives.candidate:
async forEach makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget and defeats the try/catch

Same issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: the loop was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` to await the now-async `getCalendar`, but forEach does not await async callbacks. The booking is already marked CANCELLED and the reschedule email is sent before the calendar/video event deletions complete, and any failure to delete is an unhandled rejection invisible to the surrounding try/catch. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` with individual error handling.

requestReschedule no longer awaits calendar/video deletions

In the `requestReschedule` mutation, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` was introduced because `getCalendar` became async. Since forEach doesn't await its callbacks, the mutation sends the reschedule email, fires webhooks, and returns while the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls are still pending; a serverless function may be frozen before they finish, leaving stale events on users' calendars, and any errors become unhandled rejections. Await the deletions with `Promise.all(...map(...))`.

Recurring-cancellation branch pushes into apiDeletes asynchronously after it is awaited

In the recurring-event cancellation path, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` pushes deletion promises into `apiDeletes` from async callbacks. `apiDeletes` is later consumed by `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (and by `await apiDeletes` in the paid branch), both of which run before any of these pushes happen, so the recurring calendar event deletions are never awaited and their results/errors are lost. Cancel can return success while the recurring events remain on the calendar. Collect the deletions with `Promise.all(credentials.map(...))` and push the resulting promises synchronously.

Every entry in the default-exported `appStore` map changed from a module namespace object to a `Promise` via top-level `import(...)`. This is a breaking contract change for every consumer of `@calcom/app-store`, but the PR only updates `getCalendar.ts`, `videoClient.ts`, `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, `deletePayment.ts`, and `handlePayment.ts`. Any other file that indexes `appStore[...]` synchronously (e.g. `appStore[appName].lib` or `appStore[key].app`) will now receive a Promise and silently fail checks like `"lib" in app` or crash on property access. The change needs an audit (and ideally a type-level guarantee) that all importers of `@calcom/app-store` await the values.

`log.info("calendarApp", calendarApp.lib.CalendarService)` logs the CalendarService class constructor on every calendar resolution. This runs on every booking/availability call, adding noisy, low-value log output (and potentially expensive serialization of a class). It looks like a debugging leftover and should be removed or downgraded.
